title: Fast generation of spectrally-shaped disorder, on the sphere
abstract: The design of disordered point patterns with desirable properties is an exciting and ongoing research endeavor, with applications ranging from materials to computer science. A successful approach in recent years has been the optimization of point patterns through a loss function that enforces properties in their Fourier-space representation. Yet, these methods have so far strictly been limited to flat Euclidean space, precluding their use in the contexts of coatings of curved surfaces for photonics, or of sampling of curved manifolds for instance. We introduce FaSHIoNPOp, an algorithm that relies on fast non-uniform spherical harmonics transforms, to enforce pair correlations in point patterns on the sphere with an $O(N \log N)$ complexity in $N$ the number of points. Having demonstrated its performance, we showcase applications of FaSHIoNPOp, ranging from the generation of hyperuniform structures on the sphere for sampling and physical applications, to the design of gyromorphs (disordered structures with maximal scattering power at a given frequency) on the sphere. We additionally show that FaSHIoNPOp can be combined to both global constraints like centrosymmetry, with applications to the design of more isotropic $3d$ gyromorphs, and local real-space constraints like pair repulsion. Our work paves the way for optimal sampling and coating design on curved manifolds, with many applications across physics, materials and computer science.
summary: This work presents FaSHIoNPOp, a novel algorithm for designing point patterns on the sphere by enforcing desired spectral properties using spherical harmonics. It extends powerful spectral optimization techniques from flat space to curved manifolds, enabling applications in photonics and optimal sampling. The method achieves high efficiency ($O(N \log N)$) while allowing control over complex physical properties like hyperuniformity.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of designing disordered point patterns with specific spectral properties on curved manifolds, specifically the sphere.
main_result: They introduce FaSHIoNPOp, an algorithm that successfully extends spectral optimization methods from flat Euclidean space to the sphere with $O(N \log N)$ complexity.
method: The method uses an optimization framework based on enforcing target power spectra ($S_0(\ell)$) by minimizing a loss function derived from the Spherical Harmonics Transform (SHT).
model_or_system: The system is point patterns distributed on the unit 2-sphere ($S \subset \mathbb{R}^3$). Applications include designing photonic coatings and sampling on curved manifolds.
key_observables: Power Spectrum ($S_\ell$), Radial Distribution Function ($g(	heta)$), Constraint Count ($\chi$), and Reduced Variance ($s^2$).
important_parameters: Number of points ($N$), maximum constrained mode ($\ell_{	ext{max}}$), and the target spectral coefficients ($S_0(\ell)$).
main_assumptions: The optimization relies on fast, non-uniform spherical harmonics transforms (NUSHTs) and assumes small steps during gradient-based updates, projecting positions back onto the sphere.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the algorithm flow (Initialization $	o$ SHT $	o$ Gradient $	o$ Update), and show results like the generation of hyperuniform structures ($S_\ell=0$ for $\ell \le \ell_{	ext{max}}$) and the scaling of reduced variance ($s^2$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the theory by first establishing the spectral optimization framework on the sphere, deriving the necessary gradient calculations for the loss function, and then applying this machinery to generate and characterize specific disordered states like hyperuniform structures.
why_interesting: The development of spectral optimization techniques for curved spaces provides a powerful, general tool for designing structured matter or optimal sampling configurations, which has analogues in designing quantum metamaterials or optimizing quantum state preparation.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Sketch of the algorithm. We initialize the point pattern from a Poisson point pattern on the sphere and set a target over a finite amount of ℓmodes (ℓ≤ℓmax). The power spectrum Sℓis computed using a NUSHT, then the gradients of the loss using the inverse transform (INUSHT), which is used to update positions within a gradient-based optimizer (here, L-BFGS). One such step takes O(N log N) operations. Steps are repeated until a convergence criterion is met, yielding the optimized pattern.
